hook.sub: What to sort out before your first sale.

lines: Ana booked her first art fair.
On Etsy, sales tax was handled for her.
At her own booth, it's on her.

items.s: At least 15 business days before you sell (Form NJ-REG).

items.t: Buy art materials without sales tax

beats.sub: Check the state where the fair is held.

captions.instagram:
Booked your first art fair? Sort out sales tax before the first sale, not after.

✔️ Online marketplaces like Etsy collect sales tax on sales made through them. Sales at your own booth are on you.
✔️ In New Jersey, every seller registers with the state (Form NJ-REG), at least 15 business days before starting, even seasonal sellers.
✔️ NJ sales tax is 6.625% on taxable sales.
✔️ Materials that become part of the piece, like canvas, can be bought for resale with Form ST-3. Tools like brushes can't.

Other states have their own rules, so check the state where the fair is held.

Other states have their own rules.

sources.fact: Marketplace facilitators must collect and remit NJ sales tax on sales made through their marketplace (from Nov. 1, 2018); marketplace sellers are not required to collect on those transactions (TB-83, read 2026-10-24)

All sellers, even seasonal, must register (Form NJ-REG) at least 15 business days before starting; applies at flea markets and craft shows; 6.625% rate; materials that become a component can be bought with resale certificate ST-3, supplies/tools such as paint brushes and scissors are taxable (ANJ-11 Rev. 5/25, read 2026-10-24)
